status: Component sources frozen after independent verification; integrated host verification belongs to root
problem: Native CodeEditor inferred dark mode from palette Base lightness. With a transparent QPlainTextEdit stylesheet background this can choose dark syntax on a light painted surface. The root light preview visibly contained the previous dark keyword/string/number values.

change.behavior: An explicit theme overrides automatic palette inference, rehighlights immediately and survives later PaletteChange events. EditorWidget forwards to its editor; GitPanel forwards to both read-only diff previews. Root wires existing and newly opened editors and the Git pane.
change.source_boundary: Theme APIs, token colors and comment italic style only; no Git backend, filesystem I/O, tokenizer grammar or editor lifecycle changes.

provenance.scope_note: Values are the pinned repository's shipped generated theme snapshot. Full computed CSS/personalization-color equivalence and Monaco tokenization are not claimed.

regressions: Explicit light with transparent Base uses light keyword/string/number/comment formats
Dynamic light-dark-light changes rehighlight existing text without modifying source content
Later contradictory PaletteChange does not erase explicit host theme
Both read-only Git previews receive the explicit theme
verification.environment: Independent temporary CMake build; Qt 6.11.2 static MinGW; offscreen platform. No interaction with the user's active app.

remaining_gaps: Root stylesheet globally setting Geist can override CodeEditor Roboto Mono and QFont-based zoom; reported to root separately
Existing syntax highlighter covers a subset of language categories and is not Monaco semantic-token or LSP parity
Callers that do not use the explicit theme API retain the previous palette-based fallback
